Alright, I've just finished simplifying the flushing logic in `src/tui.tsx`. Previously I was checking `if (!old.tailOnly) flushed.push(old);` to avoid flushing items that were marked as tail‑only, but I realized that this special handling is no longer necessary – the new approach just flushes everything when we exceed the budget, regardless of any `tailOnly` flag. I also updated the earlier loop that built the `live` array to stop filtering out `tailOnly` items before adding the new one. 

Given these changes, the `tailOnly` property is effectively dead code. I still have a few stray references: at line 219 I set `tailOnly: true` when constructing a tail‑only placeholder, and at line 221 I filter `liveRef.current.filter((it) => it.tailOnly)`. Those will eventually need to be cleaned up or repurposed, but the immediate TypeScript error I’m about to hit is the presence of the `tailOnly?: boolean;` field in the `Item` type definition (around line 32). Since the rest of the file no longer uses this field in any meaningful way, the type definition now contains an unused optional property, which will cause a lint warning and is just confusing for future readers.

The straightforward fix is to delete that line from the interface. I don't need to replace it with anything – just remove it entirely. I'll use the `Edit` tool to locate the exact string `"  tailOnly
